title: CSV export writes seven inheritance columns under the wrong headers (InheritUserViaAPI misalignment)
author: robertpopa22
body_snippet:
## Summary

Every CSV export (mRemoteNG format) writes seven inheritance columns under the wrong headers: the `InheritUserViaAPI` header is declared 5 positions earlier than where its value is actually emitted, shifting the whole window between them by one column.

Found during an independent model review (Codex + Gemini, both flagged it) of the CSV serializer while porting upstream features; pre-existing, not introduced by the port.

## Root cause

`CsvConnectionsSerializerMremotengFormat.cs`: ...

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet: Fixed in `83ecaf879` — the inheritance header now matches the append order (details in the commit body, item 5). Will be in the next nightly. Note: CSV files exported **before** this fix carry the shifted values for those seven columns; re-exporting after upgrading produces a correct file.

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
The fix (`83ecaf879`) is now in **[v1.83.0 stable](https://github.com/robertpopa22/mRemoteNG/releases/tag/v1.83.0)**, together with a regression test that checks the exported CSV's headers against the actual column order — a reappearance now fails the build instead of needing to be caught by eye.

Reminder from the original fix note: files exported *before* the fix carry the shifted values in those seven inheritance columns; re-exporting on 1.83.0 produces a correct file. If you can spare one ex...
